subject.title: fix(mcp): reject tools/call requests with non-object arguments

question: Should OpenClaw land the SDK-aligned Gateway MCP HTTP tightening that rejects present non-object `tools/call.params.arguments`?
rationale: The code and dependency contract support object-only arguments, but the runtime behavior change can break malformed clients that were previously tolerated, so a maintainer needs to own that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept object-only arguments
options.body: Land the PR with the existing compatibility note because the SDK contract and sibling stdio surface already require optional object arguments, and valid omitted/object calls remain covered.

options.title: Require a compatibility plan
options.body: Ask for a deprecation or compatibility plan first if maintainers know of supported clients that currently send primitive, null, or array arguments.

options.title: Pause on client evidence
options.body: Pause or close only if review surfaces a real supported OpenClaw client that depends on non-object MCP tool arguments.

recommendation.title: Accept object-only arguments
recommendation.body: Land the PR with the existing compatibility note because the SDK contract and sibling stdio surface already require optional object arguments, and valid omitted/object calls remain covered.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway MCP history and adjacent merger activity make this the clearest owner for accepting the compatibility tradeoff.
